summary: Today’s pulse tracks Stand-up comic released after being convicted of insulting Erdoğan, Trump doubles down on claims US will win war with Iran ‘one way or another’ as talks are in doubt – US politics live, and Judge sets $5m bond for third suspect in killing of Black woman hung from tree in Mississippi. Across BBC and Guardian, the strongest repeated signals are before, jones, and mississippi. In the background, Local representatives question official accounts after suspected bomb plot at RAF Fairford and Michael Wynn-Jones, husband of Delia Smith, dies aged 85 keep the wider picture in motion.

headlines.title: Stand-up comic released after being convicted of insulting Erdoğan
headlines.description: Turkish comedian Deniz Göktaş also faces a travel ban but has been released due to time served.

headlines.title: Trump doubles down on claims US will win war with Iran ‘one way or another’ as talks are in doubt – US politics live
headlines.description: President claims US negotiators spoke with Iranian officials through intermediaries after Iran says it ‘has no plans to negotiate with US’ Today, we can expect a vote at 5.30pm ET on the Protect College Sports act , which attempts to provide greater protections for university athletes in the US. The bill includes provisions for players to earn compensation from their name, image and likeness – known as NIL payments , and allow them to transfer schools (and teams) without being penalized or forced to sit out for a defined period of time. If the legislation clears the Senate it will still need to head back to the lower chamber before it can head to Donald Trump’s desk for his signature.

headlines.title: Judge sets $5m bond for third suspect in killing of Black woman hung from tree in Mississippi
headlines.description: Police said Tasia Fortune, 29, was killed before her body was placed in the tree, and the scene was ‘staged’ A Mississippi judge set a $5m bond on Monday for a third man charged in the death of a Black woman whose body was found hanging from a tree in August. Police disclosed on Friday that Tasia Fortune, 29, was killed before her body was placed in a tree behind an abandoned house in Jackson, Mississippi’s capital city.

headlines.title: Local representatives question official accounts after suspected bomb plot at RAF Fairford
headlines.description: Amid conflicting statements, local MP and councillors demand answers over how suspects were allowed to enter residential areas of nearby village An MP and councillors representing the residents of the village near RAF Fairford who were evacuated due to a suspected terror plot have expressed scepticism and concern over the security response to threats made by Iran. About 85 properties in Whelford, Gloucestershire, were evacuated on Sunday morning after five men were arrested on suspicion of explosives offences in the village. The men, who were later re-arrested on suspicion of terror offences, were released on bail on Monday.

headlines.title: Michael Wynn-Jones, husband of Delia Smith, dies aged 85
headlines.description: Former journalist and honorary life president of Norwich City FC died peacefully at home on Monday Michael Wynn-Jones, the journalist and husband of the TV chef Delia Smith, has died at the age of 85. Wynn-Jones was honorary life president of Norwich City football club, which said everyone at the club was “deeply saddened” by his death.

headlines.title: Absence of violence in Drumcree does not make standoff any less significant
headlines.description: Row comes amid rising division and a tendency towards cynical political posturing in Northern Ireland Three decades ago, it took the deaths of three Roman Catholic children – the Quinn brothers, Jason, nine, Mark, 10, and 11-year-old Richard – in a petrol bomb attack to bring an end to the Drumcree dispute. “No road is worth a life, let alone the lives of three little boys,” the Orange Order’s County Armagh chaplain said at the time. It is perhaps extraordinary to think that this could ever have needed saying – but that was then. Northern Ireland is very different place today.

headlinePool.title: Dengue fever outbreak prompts Florida counties to declare state of emergency
headlinePool.description: CDC says 392 cases of Dengue were reported for the year so far in the state, along with different county-level data Several Florida counties recently declared a state of local emergency in response to a spate of dengue fever infections. Hillsborough county, Florida, officials made the declaration on 24 September as health authorities recorded 134 confirmed cases of dengue fever, which is a mosquito-borne sickness typically found in countries outside the US. Officials said that the spread of the illness poses “an immediate and widespread threat to the public health, safety, and welfare of the residents and visitors of Hillsborough county”.

headlinePool.title: US prosecutors reopen case of alleged gang rape at Cornell University
headlinePool.description: It comes after the woman filed a civil lawsuit alleging she was drugged and raped at a fraternity house in 2024.

headlinePool.title: Questions remain over Iran’s link to alleged RAF Fairford bomb plot
headlinePool.description: Tehran has been trying to step up attacks on targets in the west but its track record has been mixed Investigators may be some way from determining exactly what led five men with three vans to a village just outside RAF Fairford in the small hours of Sunday – but the fact they have all been released on bail without immediate charge suggests they are not deemed to pose a serious and violent threat. In a moment where wider geopolitical tensions mean external threats are perceived to be close, the question of whether Iran had a hand in the alleged plot remains open. Nonetheless, the bailing of the men is a mercifully lower-key development in an investigation that appeared of the utmost gravity.

headlinePool.title: F1 in Azerbaijan: That was almost a close-run thing
headlinePool.description: Kimi Antonelli could not repeat his Monza magic after a crash in qualifying.

headlinePool.title: Arizona frat suspended after allegedly making new recruits swallow live goldfish
headlinePool.description: Case of alleged hazing at the University of Arizona is latest in series of controversial incidents involving US fraternities A college fraternity at the University of Arizona has been suspended after new members were allegedly plied with alcohol and forced to swallow live goldfish. College officials informed the university’s Sigma Tau Gamma chapter by letter earlier in September that it was under investigation for multiple alleged violations of the student code of conduct, including “endangering, threatening, or causing physical harm” to members of the campus community.

headlinePool.title: Five UK nationals arrested near RAF Fairford released on bail
headlinePool.description: Police say alleged offences could have been committed ‘knowingly or unknowingly’ on behalf of a foreign state Five men arrested over a suspected bomb plot at RAF Fairford have been released on bail as police investigate why they were so close to the airbase in three vans with suspicious material in the back. The five suspects were revealed to be British men, all in their 20s and from London. They had been arrested in the Gloucestershire countryside early on Sunday morning on suspicion of explosives offences and preparing an act of terrorism, with an Iranian link a key line of inquiry.

headlinePool.title: Twelve women have been killed in one part of South Africa since July. Here's what we know so far
headlinePool.description: South African President Cyril Ramaphosa says the murders are a "stain on our national conscience".

headlinePool.title: Century-old silent film made in New Hampshire found in Japan antique shop
headlinePool.description: Billy B Van’s 1919 comedy Van-ar-chy found by student in Sendai will be shown in early November in New Hampshire A silent comedy filmed in New Hampshire more than a century ago was recently found in Japan, and plans have been set to show the film in early November in the state where it was created. Van-ar-chy, a 1919 film starring the US entertainer and film-maker Billy B Van, was rediscovered by Kohei Okita, a film student in Sendai, Japan. While researching early cinema related to the word “anarchy”, Okita bought several old film reels at an antique store in Japan and found the comedy starring Van, whom he did not recognize, according to a Van-ar-chy news release .

headlinePool.title: Marine Le Pen hails RN senate surge as ‘milestone’ towards French presidency
headlinePool.description: National Rally and allies gain record 14 seats and can form senate group for first time after indirect vote by local officials The French far-right leader Marine Le Pen has said her 2027 presidential campaign will be boosted after her anti-immigration party, the National Rally (RN), and its allies improved to a record 14 seats in partial senate elections this weekend. Le Pen called the results a “historic victory” and a “major milestone” after her party cleared the 10-seat threshold to be able to form a senate group for the first time, after an indirect vote by local officials including mayors and councillors.
